## Tours with a Montevideo excursion from Buenos Aires

It is possible to visit Uruguay in one day during a journey that begins in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). On our [eleven-day Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/), Ada Tours leaves day three free and offers several optional outings. One possibility is a [ferry trip to Montevideo](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/).

When choosing the tour, remember that **Uruguay is an optional addition; the main itinerary is in Argentina and Brazil**. After Buenos Aires, travelers continue to El Calafate, Iguazu Falls, and the Brazilian coast at Praia de Pipa. Decide on Montevideo when arranging the itinerary rather than assuming it is included in the main tour.

## How the day trip works

Early in the morning, we organize a transfer from the hotel to the Buenos Aires ferry terminal. The ferry crosses the Río de la Plata estuary to Uruguay. Sightseeing begins at the port of [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and continues through the center and Old Town.

During the excursion, you will see Independence Square, memorials to José Gervasio Artigas, Salvo Palace, and the cathedral. Free time follows the city tour, with a return ferry and transfer back to the Buenos Aires hotel planned for the evening. **The standalone excursion lists ferry tickets, transfers, and guiding as included; lunch is excluded.** The languages offered on its page are Russian and English.

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Morning | Port and ferry crossing |
| Daytime | Historic center |
| After sightseeing | Free time |
| Return | Ferry and transfer |

Sailings, boarding times, and the duration of the free-time section depend on confirmed tickets. Before booking, calculate how many hours will actually remain in the city after both sets of border formalities and the return crossing.

## Who should add Uruguay?

This excursion appeals to travelers who want to see another capital on the opposite bank of the Río de la Plata, explore an old city, and compare Argentine and Uruguayan urban life in a short visit. The one-day focus is [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): there is no multi-day exploration of Uruguay's coastline, wineries, or Colonia del Sacramento.

If you would rather rest after an intercontinental flight, keep the free day free. The same eleven-day tour offers alternative optional excursions to Tigre and San Isidro or an introduction to gaucho traditions. Those outings do not require an international ferry crossing. Compare them with Montevideo in terms of return time, exertion, and personal interests rather than treating all options as simultaneously included.

For a more complete introduction to Uruguay, explore our [country tours](/uruguay/tour/), which devote several days to it. The [Montevideo excursion from Buenos Aires](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/) serves a different purpose: a short trip fitted into the Argentine stage of a longer journey.

## What to check before crossing

The journey involves leaving Argentina, entering Uruguay, and later returning. Document and visa requirements depend on citizenship, residency status, and whether re-entry to Argentina is permitted. Even if a country permits visa-free entry, the conditions of the return crossing must be checked separately.

Besides passport requirements, clarify luggage arrangements and how early to arrive before ferry departure. The itinerary includes boarding, border control, and travel from the hotel to the terminal. Ferry schedules may change with weather conditions. We can help coordinate the crossing with the following day's main-program flight to Patagonia.

## Frequently asked questions about Montevideo

### Is Montevideo included in the eleven-day tour's main route?

No. On the [Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/), day three is reserved for rest or optional excursions. Montevideo is one of the available choices.

### Can I visit Montevideo without staying overnight?

Yes. The [standalone excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/) is a full-day trip with a return ferry to Buenos Aires. Confirm sailing times, border procedures, and the return time before booking.

### What does the standalone excursion include?

According to the Ada Tours description, it includes transfers, ferry tickets, and a guide; lunch costs extra. Whether the optional excursion is covered by the wider tour price depends on the chosen arrangements and must be agreed when booking.

## Walking tour of Montevideo's historic center

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is best discovered on foot in its old quarters. The main squares, colonial buildings, and cultural landmarks are close enough for travelers to experience the area as a connected history. The Ada Tours walking excursion lasts **four hours** and moves from the central public spaces toward Ciudad Vieja, the historic heart of Uruguay's capital.

The route includes Liberty Square, 18 de Julio Avenue, Independence Square, the Citadel Gate, pedestrian Sarandí Street, the Metropolitan Cathedral, and other landmarks such as Solís Theatre. It suits anyone who wants to examine the architecture and walk the old streets rather than seeing the city solely through a car window.

## Independence Square and the Citadel Gate

Independence Square helps explain Montevideo's history. It contains a monument to José Artigas, one of the country's most important historical figures, while the striking Palacio Salvo rises nearby. The palace tower has long been a recognizable part of the city skyline.

The Citadel Gate recalls the time when the colonial settlement was enclosed by fortifications. When the main defenses were demolished in the 19th century, new open urban spaces developed. The arrangement of the square and old streets illustrates the transition from fortified settlement to the capital of an independent nation.

Almost at a single crossroads, different eras of the city can be explored. Take time to consider how monuments, thoroughfares, and historic buildings relate to one another.

## Sarandí Street, cathedral, and the monument to Zabala

Beyond the gate lies Ciudad Vieja. Pedestrian Sarandí Street leads into neighborhoods with surviving urban buildings and squares in the historic center. The contrast between the broad spaces of newer Montevideo and the more intimate streets of the old town becomes clear here.

The Metropolitan Cathedral, also known as the Matriz, and the monument to Bruno Mauricio de Zabala introduce the city's religious heritage and early history. The stops form a coherent sequence for first-time visitors to Uruguay. However, **mentioning a landmark on the route does not automatically include paid admission** or a tour of all its interiors.

Solís Theatre is another important stop. Opened in 1856, it became a symbol of the young capital's cultural development. Its history forms part of the Old Town walk; a separate interior tour or performance ticket is not specified as included.

## What is included and what does it cost?

The excursion includes an English-speaking guide and transfers. **Lunch is not included.** With a four-hour duration, it is convenient as one part of a day, leaving time for other activities afterward.

| Rate | Price |
|---|---|
| Standard price | $280 |
| Group of 2–4 people | $141 per person |

These prices apply specifically to our walking tour. Ada Tours may adjust the sequence of stops while retaining the main sights. Agree on the meeting time, transfer limits, and any additional admission tickets when booking.

## Walking tour or general city sightseeing?

We also offer a different program: the [four-hour Montevideo city tour and historic center](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-city-old-town-tour/). It covers a broader area, including the Rambla, markets, monuments, and Carrasco, and includes lunch at Mercado del Puerto.

The walking excursion concentrates on the historic district around Sarandí Street and the Old Town landmarks. **Rates and meal arrangements differ between these products**, so the same duration does not make them interchangeable.

For a longer journey through [Uruguay](/uruguay/), add a day on the [Piriápolis and Punta Ballena coast](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Montevideo walking tour

### How long does the walking excursion take?

It lasts four hours. Agree on the exact starting and finishing points along with the transfer.

### Is lunch included?

No. Lunch is explicitly listed among the services excluded from the walking itinerary.

### Is an English-speaking guide provided?

Yes. The itinerary specifies an English-speaking guide.

### Can we go inside Solís Theatre?

The theater appears as a stop, but admission and an interior tour have not been separately confirmed. Ask about an interior visit when booking.

### How does this product differ from the other city tour?

The walking route focuses primarily on Ciudad Vieja. The wider city tour covers more neighborhoods and includes lunch, so the two offerings have different itineraries and prices.

## Punta del Este and Piriápolis from Montevideo

A day trip from [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) can introduce travelers to several very different seaside towns in Uruguay. Piriápolis is known for its historic resort architecture, Punta Ballena for the white forms of Casapueblo overlooking the ocean, and Punta del Este for its beaches, yachting facilities, and modern neighborhoods.

The Ada Tours excursion lasts **eight hours**. Travelers depart Montevideo for Piriápolis, then visit Punta Ballena and Punta del Este. An optional winery stop is possible on the return. This is a coastal excursion, not a sightseeing tour of the capital itself.

## Piriápolis: the historic seaside resort

[Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) is associated with the early development of resort tourism in Uruguay. Its broad bay, waterfront promenade, and historic buildings helped shape the seaside town's character.

The itinerary includes a drive along Rambla Costanera, an introduction to the historic Gran Hotel Argentino, and an ascent of San Antonio Hill. The elevated viewpoint reveals the coastline and town. Views depend on weather and visibility, so photographs cannot be expected to look identical in every season.

This stage reveals a side of Uruguay where the history of seaside holidays is reflected in town planning, hotels, and waterfront walks.

## Punta Ballena and Casapueblo

The next stop is [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/), home to Casapueblo, a white building with intricate terraces created by the artist Carlos Páez Vilaró. Its unusual architecture developed gradually through the artist's work over many years.

Today, Casapueblo is known for its museum and art gallery featuring the artist's work. The venue's own website describes paintings, ceramics, sculptures, and open terraces overlooking the coast. **Casapueblo's presence on the Ada Tours route does not confirm that a separate museum admission ticket is included**, or that guests can attend special museum events. If you wish to see the interior collection, agree on the visit beforehand.

Allow time for at least the distinctive exterior and its rocky coastal surroundings. This stop offers something quite different from other resort facades.

## Punta del Este: a town on a peninsula

The journey continues to Punta del Este. On our excursion, you drive through residential districts with mansions and landscaped gardens, and along the waterfront with its well-known hotels.

Punta del Este differs from Piriápolis through its modern resort facilities. The combination of ocean coastline and city life, varied beaches, and views across the peninsula make it appealing.

The sightseeing format allows for several stops, not a full day devoted to swimming at one beach. If you want to swim or spend several hours relaxing by the sea, arrange a different balance of activities in advance.

## Optional winery on the way back

On the return, guests may choose to stop at the **Alta Bageña winery**. Importantly, **wine tasting is not included** in the basic excursion price. Mentioning the winery does not promise a prepaid tasting or a tour of the production facilities.

**Lunch is also excluded.** The timing of a possible stop, tasting availability, and final price must be agreed separately. If wine is not of interest, this excursion can be enjoyed as a journey through seaside towns and landscapes.

## Price, guiding language, and arrangements

| Condition | Ada Tours details |
|---|---|
| Duration | 8 hours |
| Standard price | $953 |
| Group of 2–4 people | $477 per person |
| Guide | English-speaking |
| Transfers | Included |
| Wine tasting | Not included |
| Lunch | Not included |

The order of visits may change while preserving the itinerary. Explore other destinations on our [Uruguay page](/uruguay/), or book a [historic-center walking tour](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-old-town-walking-tour/) for a closer look at the capital.

## Frequently asked questions about Piriápolis and Punta del Este

### How long is the trip from Montevideo?

The excursion lasts eight hours, including travel and the main sightseeing stops.

### Is a winery visit included?

An optional stop at Alta Bageña can be arranged, while wine tasting is paid for separately.

### Is lunch included?

No. Lunch is excluded from the excursion.

### Can we visit the Casapueblo museum?

Casapueblo is on the route. Arrange museum admission, time for viewing the collection, and tickets separately before departure.

### Is this a Montevideo city tour?

No. The focus is the resort coast: Piriápolis, Punta Ballena, and Punta del Este. The trip starts and ends in Montevideo.

## Excursions to Piriápolis: what is included and how to choose

You can visit [Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) on an excursion along Uruguay's southern coast. Our itinerary travels **from Montevideo via Piriápolis and Punta Ballena to Punta del Este**. This is convenient if you want to see several coastal places in one day without spending the night at a resort.

The main point to remember is that **the excursion passes through Piriápolis but is not devoted solely to it**. There are several different stretches of coast to see in a day. If you prefer leisurely walks, beaches, and separate trips into the hills, allow the resort more time.

## What you will see in Piriápolis on an Ada Tours itinerary

The [Punta del Este and Piriápolis excursion from Montevideo](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/) includes these stops:

- **Rambla Costanera:** a coastal road overlooking the curve of the beach. It reveals the layout of the historic resort stretching along the waterfront.
- **Argentino Hotel:** a historic hotel built during the development of the resort by Francisco Piria. We introduce travelers to its architecture; a visit to the interior is not separately promised.
- **San Antonio Hill:** views over the bay, harbor, Piriápolis buildings, and green hills. This is an excellent viewpoint for understanding the resort's geography.

After Piriápolis, the journey continues to [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/) and then [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). An optional winery stop may be arranged. Tasting is not included in the basic rate.

The excursion lasts **eight hours**. We provide an English-speaking guide and transfers, while lunch is paid for separately. Check the conditions, price, and group size on the [excursion's own page](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/) rather than carrying rates across between different versions of a program.

## A day trip or several days in Piriápolis?

| Format | When it works best |
|---|---|
| Excursion from Montevideo | You want to see several resorts in one day |
| Overnight stay | Beaches and relaxed walks matter most |
| A day devoted to the town | You want to explore its surroundings more thoroughly |

The **excursion from [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/)** saves you the need to arrange transfers between coastal towns independently. But travel and other stops limit time in Piriápolis itself. Staying at the resort lets you choose when to walk the waterfront, return to viewpoints, and plan a beach day around the weather.

Our [Piriápolis destination guide](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) covers attractions in and around the town. Here, we focus on excursions that genuinely include Piriápolis on their itineraries.

## What else can you add if you have more time?

Beyond a short coastal visit, Francisco Piria's castle, associated with the town's founder, and walks in the hills deserve attention. Cerro Pan de Azúcar also lies near the town. However, **these places are not confirmed stops on our eight-hour excursion**: they are separate ideas for a longer stay, requiring additional transport and time.

Travelers interested primarily in the sea can set aside some time for the central beach and promenade. The Southern Hemisphere summer brings more visitors to the coast, so plans should reflect seasonal demand. In cooler months, architecture and viewpoints may be more rewarding than an extended beach day.

## Piriápolis and Punta Ballena on the same route

Although both stops lie on Uruguay's southern coastline, they offer different experiences. **Piriápolis** is a historic seaside resort with a long promenade, older buildings, and a hilltop viewpoint. **[Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/)** is known above all for its headland and Casapueblo, the house-museum of artist Carlos Páez Vilaró.

The combined excursion allows visitors to compare both in one day. But entering Casapueblo, purchasing a museum ticket, or attending a sunset ceremony should not be assumed to be included because the tour stops at the headland. If the museum is your main goal, agree on the visit's duration and return time in advance.

When designing your own trip, you can divide [Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/), [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/), and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) across different days to spend more time on your preferred activities. For a single day from the capital, there is already a [ready-made Ada Tours excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/).

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Piriápolis

### Where does the excursion through Piriápolis start?

Our eight-hour excursion starts in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). It visits Piriápolis, Punta Ballena, and Punta del Este; it is not a separate excursion departing from Piriápolis.

### Can I see Piriápolis in one day?

Yes. A short visit on the combined excursion covers the waterfront, historic hotel, and panorama from San Antonio Hill. For beaches and additional walks, allow more time.

### Is San Antonio Hill included?

Yes, San Antonio Hill is on the [excursion route](/uruguay/montevideo/punta-del-este-piriapolis-from-montevideo/). The way up and order of stops depend on the day's arrangements.

### Are lunch and wine tasting included?

No. Both are excluded from our basic itinerary. A winery visit is optional and must be arranged separately.

### Where can I find all excursions through Piriápolis?

This page gathers excursions that visit Piriápolis. For the full itinerary and applicable terms, open the specific excursion page; for the town itself, see our [Piriápolis guide](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/).

## Bouza Winery in Uruguay: vineyards and gastronomy near Montevideo

**Bodega Bouza**, or Bouza Winery, is located in the rural Melilla district near [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). It is a convenient choice for travelers wanting to experience Uruguayan wine production while staying near the capital. Rather than driving across the country, you can set aside part of a day for vineyards, the cellar, an introduction to grape varieties, and lunch.

Bouza's main appeal is the link between winemaking and gastronomy. Visitors learn how grapes are grown and how the winery operates, then compare different wines alongside food. It is an excellent complement to a cultural itinerary in the capital, especially if you want to explore beyond city streets.

## Where is Bodega Bouza, and why is it convenient?

The winery lies in **Melilla**, northwest of central Montevideo. Its official address is Camino de la Redención 7658 bis. Although it belongs geographically to the greater capital area, the surroundings are rural, with grape-growing land.

This makes it possible to divide a day between two different experiences: explore historic Montevideo in the morning and devote the rest of the day to the winery. Driving time depends on your hotel, transport, and traffic. Do not assume a standard winery transfer is included without checking the conditions of your particular excursion.

Bouza also runs other dining venues, including **Las Espinas in Maldonado Department** and **Bouza Vinos & Tapas in Punta del Este**. This is an important distinction when booking: a Bouza wine bar or restaurant on the coast is a different place, and visiting it is not the same as touring the main winery in Melilla.

## What can you learn on a winery tour?

### Vineyards and estate production

Bouza states that it uses grapes from its own vineyards. A visit therefore provides an opportunity to follow the journey from vines to production facilities. During a walk, discuss grape varieties, growing conditions, seasonal plant care, and how harvest results influence the finished wine.

**Tannat** has a special place in Uruguay and is widely associated with the country's winemaking. Bouza works with other red and white varieties too, including Albariño. The wines available for tasting depend on the chosen offering and current selection.

During a tour of the production facilities, it is worth exploring how grape quality is monitored, why different batches undergo different processes, and where agriculture gives way to the winemaker's craft. That is far more revealing than simply listing the names on bottle labels.

### Tastings and food pairings

Gastronomy is a significant part of Bouza's approach. Different wine-tasting and restaurant experiences are offered. The restaurant uses Uruguayan and international cooking techniques, while pairings help guests compare how food changes their perception of a wine.

One appeal of the winery is **matching a particular wine to a particular dish**, rather than discussing aroma in isolation. Meat, vegetables, cheeses, and lighter dishes call for different combinations. If you do not drink alcohol, check the food-focused program and available alternatives beforehand.

It is important to distinguish a winery tour, a separate tasting, a restaurant menu, and a combined package. They may have different terms and prices. The existence of an on-site restaurant does not mean lunch is included in every admission.

### Garage and its classic-car collection

Bouza also has an area called **Garage**, dedicated to the family's collection of classic cars and motorcycles. Official winery materials describe this as part of the visitor experience.

It is an enjoyable extra for anyone interested in vehicles and motoring history. But entry to the Garage or a tasting inside it depends on the chosen visit format. When organizing your itinerary, confirm which parts of the collection are accessible on your date.

## Bouza or Garzón: which winery should you choose?

Travelers in Uruguay often compare **Bouza** with **[Garzón](/uruguay/place/garzon-winery/)**. Both introduce the country's wine culture, but their locations and trip logistics differ.

| Winery | Convenient starting point |
|---|---|
| Bouza | Montevideo |
| Garzón | Punta del Este |

Bouza is well suited to an outing near the capital combining winemaking and lunch. Garzón is in Maldonado Department, closer to routes along the Atlantic coast, and offers separate vineyard walks, tastings, and gastronomic experiences.

Base your choice on the actual location and your travel plans, not an abstract ranking of wineries. If you will only visit Montevideo, heading to Melilla usually makes more sense. If you have several nights in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), you can also allow time for Garzón.

## What time of year should you go?

Seasons in the Southern Hemisphere are the opposite of those in Europe. Vines are dormant in winter, a new growth cycle begins in spring, vineyards become especially green in summer, and harvest normally falls in late summer or early autumn. Exact dates depend on weather and the grape variety.

A winery can also be visited outside the harvest. Cellar operations, explanations of winemaking, and restaurant experiences do not depend entirely on ripe grapes being on the vines. However, seeing the harvest itself is possible only in season and when the estate allows visitors to observe the work.

When choosing dates, be aware that tours and restaurant tables may require advance reservations. Wear comfortable shoes for outdoor walks and bring sun protection, plus a light jacket in cooler months.

## Bouza Winery on an Ada Tours itinerary

Our ["Best of Uruguay: Five-Star Tour"](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/) visits Bouza on **day three**, after sightseeing in Montevideo. The itinerary includes a tour of the winery and vineyards, followed by **a three-course lunch with wine pairings**. Travelers return to their hotel the same day.

These are services included in that particular tour. They do not mean that every Bouza visitor automatically receives the same lunch without booking. The same six-day itinerary travels on to Punta del Este and, on another day, visits [Garzón Winery](/uruguay/place/garzon-winery/), allowing guests to compare two different wine estates on one journey.

If gastronomy is a main reason for your trip, explore [Uruguay tours](/uruguay/tour/) and [food and wine journeys through Uruguay](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/). Check each actual itinerary for included tastings and meals: even two tours in the same country may differ substantially.

## Practical advice for visiting

A winery visit is best enjoyed with time for questions, a walk, and a relaxed meal. Agree on the duration, touring language, transport to Melilla, and return journey in advance. If you are driving, alcohol tasting is incompatible with driving afterward: arrange a designated driver or other transport.

If you have dietary restrictions, discuss the menu ahead of time, particularly for a set multi-course lunch. Having a restaurant on site does not guarantee every dish can be changed without prior arrangements.

Also confirm whether you are booking **the main Bodega Bouza in Melilla** or another Bouza venue on the coast. This avoids address confusion and lets the winery fit smoothly into your route.

## Frequently asked questions about Bouza Winery

### Where is the main Bodega Bouza located?

In Melilla near Montevideo, Uruguay. This is not the same as the Bouza restaurant in Punta del Este.

### Can I visit Bouza without lunch?

The winery offers different tour and tasting formats. Choose the precise services when booking; a restaurant lunch is not mandatory for every option.

### What is the Bouza Garage?

A separate area holding the Bouza family's collection of classic cars and motorcycles. Access depends on the tour format you choose.

### How is Bouza different from Garzón?

Primarily in location and logistics. Bouza is near Montevideo, while Garzón is convenient for itineraries based around Punta del Este.

### Is Bouza included in existing Ada Tours itineraries?

Yes. A visit with a three-course lunch is included in our current [six-day Uruguay tour](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/).
